key_insight: Interface orientation tunes heat transfer in lateral MoSe₂/MoS₂ heterostructures, with extrapolated armchair conductance about 22% higher than zigzag conductance.
engineering_relevance: Choosing interface orientation offers a route to controlling heat dissipation in 2D nanoelectronic and optoelectronic junctions.
method: Train a DeePMD-kit deep learning interatomic potential on DFT data.
Validate against DFT energies, forces, and phonon dispersions.
Run non-equilibrium molecular dynamics for armchair and zigzag interfaces over 10–40 nm cell lengths.
evidence_signal: Infinite-length extrapolation yields 473 MW/m²K for armchair versus 387 MW/m²K for zigzag interfaces; at 300 K, armchair interfaces also show greater phonon spectral overlap.
watch_item: The reported conductances rely on finite-size extrapolation, and the abstract reports no experimental validation.
paper_title: Orientation-Tunable Interfacial Thermal Conductance in Lateral MoSe2/MoS2 Heterostructures: A Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics Study
